links.outcome: Weighted LLM-judge score of multi-agent versus single-agent configuration on the same queries
links.effect: Weighted LLM-judge score rose from 1.695 to 1.797 (p = 0.027); three other judges showed gains of +0.111 to +0.186 (all p < 0.05). Medical safety did not differ.
links.quote: The Multi Agent improved the weighted LLM-judge score from 1.695 to 1.797 (p = 0.027), and three additional LLM judges showed consistent improvements ($Δ$ = +0.111 to +0.186, all p < 0.05).

unlisted_practices: Multi-agent decomposition of compound queries into intent-specific agents with parallel execution and synthesis
Evaluating latency and cost trade-offs of multi-agent LLM orchestration

screen.reason: Evaluates a novel multi-agent LLM system vs. single-agent baseline on synthetic health checkup queries; comparing agent architectures is model/system development rather than testing a health care deployment guardrail.
